eyebrow: Python for Data Engineers · Chapter 1, Lesson 3
subtitle: Cleaning messy text and building readable output — tools you'll use in nearly every lesson from here on.

code:
region = "West"
product = 'Trail Runner GTX'

full_description = region + " — " + product
print(full_description)   # West — Trail Runner GTX

status = "Shipped"
print(status[0])     # 'S'
print(status[0:4])    # 'Ship'
caption: + concatenates strings. Indexing starts at 0, and a slice runs up to (not including) the end.

code:
raw_status = "  shipped \n"

cleaned = raw_status.strip()        # "shipped"
normalized = cleaned.upper()        # "SHIPPED"

product_name = "Trail Runner GTX"
safe_name = product_name.replace(" ", "_")   # "Trail_Runner_GTX"
caption: .strip() matters most once you read real files — every line carries an invisible trailing newline.

eyebrow: .split() — pulling fields out of a raw line
code:
raw_line = "1002,502,Marcus Ibeh,East,Alpine 2P Tent,Camping,1,249.50,2026-01-04,Shipped"

fields = raw_line.split(",")
order_id = fields[0]
customer_name = fields[2]
status = fields[9]
print(order_id, customer_name, status)
caption: Every field comes back as a string — fields[0] is "1002", not the number 1002.

code:
customer_name = "Priya Nandan"
quantity = 1
product = "Trail Runner GTX"

summary = f"{customer_name} ordered {quantity}x {product}"
print(summary)

unit_price = 129.99
print(f"Unit price: ${unit_price:.2f}")   # Unit price: $129.99
caption: :.2f formats a float with exactly 2 decimal places — the standard way to display currency.
